_README: Copy this to config.json (npm run init does it for you) and replace the fields below with your own. lat/lon are decimal degrees — longitude is NEGATIVE in the western hemisphere. Everything else has working defaults.
_fieldsComment: farm is optional and free-form — group fields by operation, landlord, or whoever you scout for, and the dashboard gains a farm filter. Fields with no farm show up under "No farm set".

gauges._comment: How many nearby gauges each field lists, and how many of them count without being asked. One pair of numbers across every fetched network, replacing the old per-network maxStations. Unticking a gauge does NOT promote the next one into its place — the list is the nearest N by distance and nothing else, because being handed a gauge thirty miles away in exchange for one half a mile away is a different measurement of different ground wearing the same name. Everything listed keeps its history either way, so ticking one back on restores it.

region._comment: Leave states empty and it is auto-detected from your field coordinates on `npm run init` / `npm run discover`, then written back here. Set it manually to override.

iemre.label: MRMS / PRISM gridded (IEM Reanalysis)
iemre._comment: ~12km grid, CONUS-wide, with full historical backfill. The backbone of the archive.

rfcqpe.label: RFC QPE 4km (NWS multi-sensor)
rfcqpe._comment: ~4km grid — the finest source here that needs no GRIB toolchain. SNAPSHOT ONLY: publishes rolling windows with no archive, so it cannot backfill and a missed daily run loses that day permanently. dayOffset files the 24h-ending-12Z product against a local day; -1 is an informed default. Verify with `npm run check` after ~30 days and adjust if the correlation peak is not at lag 0.

iem_gauge.label: NWS COOP + ASOS gauges
iem_gauge._comment: Leave networks empty to auto-derive <STATE>_COOP and <STATE>_ASOS from the detected region. These cover the whole US. maxDistanceKm is how far out to look; how many are kept and how many count is `gauges` above.

ksmesonet.label: Kansas Mesonet
ksmesonet._comment: Kansas only — skipped automatically outside KS. Research-grade gauges, denser than COOP where it applies.

manual.label: Manual gauges
manual._comment: Gauges somebody reads by hand — a stick gauge by the shop, a neighbour's gauge near a field. Nothing fetches these; readings are typed into the dashboard and are never overwritten by an ingest. They rank by distance like any other station but are charted as their own series, so they stay an independent check instead of being averaged into the automatic gauge figure. Add them from the dashboard rather than by hand.

weatherlink.label: On-farm weather station
weatherlink._comment: For a Davis (or any station) publishing WeatherLink's NOAA-format reports. Add it from the dashboard rather than by hand — "Your own weather station" tests the two URLs and reads the station's coordinates out of the report header, which prints them in deg/min/sec. lat/lon must be the STATION's position, not a field's. This becomes ground truth and drives `npm run calibrate`. NOTE: NOAAMO.txt holds only the current month and is overwritten at month roll, so daily history accumulates from your first run — run the ingest at least monthly.
weatherlink.name: My Farm Station

season._comment: calendar = Jan 1 totals (US ag convention). water = Oct 1 (western US hydrology convention).

updates._comment: If this copy was installed with git and git is on the machine, the dashboard checks once a day whether newer code has been published, and offers a button to download it and restart. Nothing is ever applied without being asked. The update is fast-forward only and refuses outright if there are local edits, so it can never leave a merge conflict behind. Set enabled to false to stop checking.

ingest._revisitComment: Re-fetch the last N days every run. PRISM and COOP reports get revised after publication, so recent days are not final.
ingest._autoComment: The dashboard collects rainfall itself while it is running: every 15 minutes it checks whether the last run is older than intervalHours and pulls if so. Catch-up rather than clock scheduling, because a farm computer is off as often as it is on and a fixed 7:15 task on a machine that boots at 9 simply never runs. Set auto to false only if you would rather drive it from a scheduled task and `npm run ingest`.
